newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Laporte sees sharp drop in profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Laporte sees sharp drop in profit.

text.p: Profits at specialty chemicals group Laporte Plc plunged in the first half of the year, but the company promised that its 31 million pound ($48.11 million) recovery programme was on target.
Luton-based Laporte said first-half pre-tax profit slid to 36.4 million pounds from 67.0 million a year before.
Losses of nearly 24.0 million pounds on a series of disposals were responsible for the lion's share of the decline.
But tough market conditions, particularly in Europe, also played a part, and Laporte opted to freeze its interim dividend at 8.5 pence.

Shares in the group, which issued a profit warning and announced plans for a major overhaul last December, responded favourably to the results, which were towards the top of analysts' expectations. The shares were five pence higher at 747 late morning.

Analysts welcomed signs that the restructuring, which includes getting rid of a string of non-core activities, is on course to achieve annual cost-savings of 10 million pounds next year, but they were concerned at continued weakness in Europe.
In a telephone interview, chief executive Jim Leng said the reorganisation was "on budget, on time and delivering the benefits we said."

Laporte announced another set of small-scale disposals on Monday, bringing the total achieved so far this year to 60 million pounds. Leng estimated that businesses worth around 20 million pound remain to be sold.

Raw material costs, which were key to a disappointing performance across the industry in the second half of 1995, have stabilized at lower levels, and Leng said he expects prices to "trend along those lines" for the rest of the year.
He declined to go beyond Laporte's formula of forecasting "solid progress" for 1996 as a whole amid continued competitive pressures and subdued trading in some markets.

"We are heading in the right direction," Leng said. "We fired on three and a half cylinders out of five in the first half." Laporte said the full-year dividend would be based on general progress, a stance that Leng said was "realistic."

Problems in bulk polymers continued to hit Laporte's specialty organics division, where trading profits slid 37 percent. The star performer was compounds and electronics, where profits jumped 45 percent.
With disposals almost completed, Laporte was now in a position to think about fresh acquisitions, Leng said, with the Far East, Europe and North America all favoured targets.
"We are thinking about other moves now," Leng said. "We are looking for market leadership and focus on growth sectors." ($1=.6444 Pound)
